MEMORANDUM (PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL) - TO: Rachel Stein-Nakamura, General Counsel, Verdana Technologies, Inc. RE: Statute of limitations for breach of contract claims against Crestline Systems Group, LLC (ERP integration). AS-OF NOTE: The latest matter document is the August 30, 2022 email. This memo is written as of early September 2022. If it is being read later (the system date is October 2, 2026), the contractual deadlines below have long passed; confirm immediately whether suit was filed or a signed tolling agreement exists.

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) New York law governs (MSA 14.3, with NY GOL 5-1401 recital) and the MSA 14.7 bars any action brought more than 18 months after accrual. New York enforces a reasonable, shorter, written limitations period (CPLR 201; Kassner v. City of New York, 46 N.Y.2d 544 (1979)). 18 months from accrual, re-ratified in Amendment No. 1 7.2(f), is likely enforceable. Plan on 14.7, not the six-year CPLR 213(2) period.
(b) The Board memo's window (January 22, 2023 to August 4, 2023) is not safe. The earliest defensible deadline is about December 30, 2022 (18 months from the June 30, 2021 missed delivery date). The latest date, August 4, 2023 (second notice), is wrong because a notice letter is not a breach and Verdana knew the facts by January 28, 2022.
(c) No tolling exists. The June 14-17, 2022 emails were a proposal and a noncommittal reply. MSA 14.5 says negotiation and mediation do not toll absent a separate signed writing. The Board declined to authorize tolling on July 12, 2022, and your August 30, 2022 email confirmed no tolling and ended talks.
(d) Mediation (14.5) is a condition precedent to suit and must run at least 60 days, untolled. To file by December 30, 2022, the written mediation notice must be delivered (per 13.2) no later than about October 31, 2022. Recommend sending it now.

2. GOVERNING FRAMEWORK
- Statutory default: six years for contract, CPLR 213(2); accrual at breach, regardless of knowledge or damage (Ely-Cruikshank Co. v. Bank of Montreal, 81 N.Y.2d 399 (1993)).
- Contractual shortening: enforceable if in writing and reasonable (CPLR 201; Kassner). Executive Plaza, LLC v. Peerless Ins. Co., 22 N.Y.3d 511 (2014), voids a period only where it is unreasonable in operation, such as expiring before the claim could be brought. Risk argument for Verdana: 14.5 forces at least 60 days of untolled mediation first. That consumes about 11% of the 18 months and, in my view, will not make the period unreasonable.
- UCC alternative: if Article 2 applied (predominant-purpose test), the period is four years, reducible by agreement to not less than one year but not extendable; accrual is tender of delivery regardless of knowledge, July 22, 2021 (N.Y. UCC 2-725). Under that regime 18 months is permissible and the date would be about January 22, 2023 (likely the origin of the Board memo date). Verdana's own Acceptance Test Report stresses that 20 of 23 Sev 1 defects sit in packaged products, which invites a goods characterization. Counterpoints: the MSA is a phased custom design-and-development services contract (Arts. 2-3, Exhibit A), Verdana owns the Work Product (6.1), and fees are phase-based. I assess services (CPLR) as more likely, but UCC risk is a reason to use the earlier date. Also, a clause deferring accrual past tender could be attacked as an impermissible extension under 2-725(1). Unresolved.
- Texas contrary rule: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code 16.070 voids contractual limitation periods shorter than two years. Verdana is in Austin, but the NY choice-of-law clause and exclusive New York County forum clause (14.4) make this a weak lever. Suing in Texas would breach 14.4 and invite dismissal. Not a basis for planning.
- Borrowing statute risk to the fallback period: Verdana is a nonresident of New York; a purely economic contract injury accrues where the plaintiff resides (Global Financial Corp. v. Triarc Corp., 93 N.Y.2d 525 (1999)), and CPLR 202 requires timeliness under both NY and that jurisdiction's period. A generic choice-of-law clause does not displace CPLR 202 (Portfolio Recovery Assocs. v. King, 14 N.Y.3d 410 (2010)). Texas's general contract period is, to my understanding, four years (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code 16.051; not primary-source verified here). So the statutory fallback may be about four years (July 2025 onward), not the six years in the Board memo (2027-2028). This matters only if 14.7 fails.

3. CLAIMS AND ACCRUAL (conservative first)
(1) Late Phase 3 delivery. Amended deadline June 30, 2021 (Amendment 2.1); delivered July 22, 2021. Breach occurred on or about July 1, 2021. 14.7 accrual is when Verdana knew; it knew then. 18 months: about December 30, 2022. This is the controlling outside date. The Board memo used July 22, 2021 (January 22, 2023); that is wrong for the delay claim itself, though right for a UCC tender theory.
(2) Defective/nonconforming Phase 3 deliverable and failure of acceptance criteria (MSA 3.4, 7.2(b), Exhibit B). Verdana's testing began September 13, 2021; the Final Acceptance Test failed October 3, 2021 (report October 5). Crestline will argue knowledge on or about those dates: roughly March 13 to April 3, 2023. Verdana's counter: under 3.4 a first test failure is not itself a material breach; only failure of a second test is, so accrual is the January 17-28, 2022 retest result, about July 28, 2023.
(3) Failure to cure under 9.2. Cure period ended about January 16, 2022 (90 days from the October 18 notice date). Strictly, the clock runs from receipt: FedEx overnight is deemed delivered one business day after deposit (13.2(b)), about October 19, giving January 17; Crestline acknowledged receipt October 22, giving January 20. Eighteen months: about July 16 to 20, 2023. Use July 14, 2023 conservatively.
(4) Warranty claims 7.2(b), (f). 7.2(f) speaks "upon Final Acceptance," which never occurred; accrual arguments are later but uncertain. Do not rely on them.
(5) Phase 2 delay (June 30 to August 14, 2020): barred. Amendment 6.3 states Verdana has no outstanding claims on Phase 2, and 18 months expired by February 2022. Do not plead.
(6) Indemnity 10.1: covers third-party claims only; not a vehicle for direct losses.
Recommended working rule: treat December 30, 2022 as the last day to be in court for all claims, which makes mediation initiation by October 31, 2022 the real deadline. Plead all theories together; a later-accruing theory is a fallback only.

4. NO TOLLING; ESTOPPEL IS WEAK
- GOL 17-103 requires a post-accrual written promise signed by the promisor. 14.5 and 13.5 reinforce writing and signature requirements. None exists: Crestline asked for tolling and offered to draft a letter; Verdana replied it was evaluating; the Board declined; the August 30 email disclaims tolling.
- Equitable estoppel requires specific, deceptive conduct by the defendant that induced the plaintiff to refrain from suing, and reasonable reliance (Zumpano v. Quinn, 6 N.Y.3d 666 (2006)). Crestline made no assurance that it would not plead the limitations period; its emails said the opposite ("without a tolling agreement in place, both parties may need to consider their respective positions"). Verdana disclaimed tolling twice. Estoppel is not a viable plan.
- Practical fix: if tolling is still wanted, a signed bilateral agreement must be executed before the earliest deadline; it cannot revive claims already barred. The Board's July 12 decision should be revisited now that talks have ended; the Board memo's retroactive tolling concept helps only if Crestline signs before expiry.

5. PRECONDITIONS AND PROCEDURE
- 14.1/14.2: informal negotiation notice; escalation after 30 days. Permissive ("may"); the March to August 2022 talks arguably satisfy it, but send a short 14.1 notice with the mediation notice to remove any argument.
- 14.5: written notice proposing mediation services; 10 business days to agree, else JAMS or AAA, in New York City; 60-day minimum participation; a senior representative with authority. Non-compliant suits may be stayed or dismissed. If the suit is dismissed for failure to mediate, rescue under CPLR 205(a) is uncertain for a contractual period; do not rely on it.
- Forum: state or federal court in New York County (14.4). File with the Supreme Court, New York County, or the Southern District of New York (diversity depends on Crestline LLC members' citizenship, unknown). Commencement is by filing (CPLR 304), followed by service within 120 days (CPLR 306-b).

6. CRESTLINE'S COUNTERCLAIMS AND THE BOARD MEMO
- The Board memo assumes Crestline's fee claims accrued at July 22, 2021 or January 16, 2022. That appears wrong. Under MSA 5.2 and Amendment 3.3 and 4, fees are due only after acceptance; the Phase 4 fee is due only after Phase 4, and the $375,000 change-order fee only 30 days after written acceptance. No acceptance exists. Crestline's accrual would instead come from an alleged anticipatory repudiation (its February 18, 2022 letter points to Verdana's refusal to proceed), about August 2023 at the earliest under 14.7. Crestline would also argue prevention of conditions. So the Board should not assume Crestline's counterclaims lapse earlier than Verdana's claims.
- CPLR 203(d): even a time-barred counterclaim arising from the same transaction survives as a recoupment defense up to the amount of the complaint's demand. Whether a contractual period limits 203(d) is unresolved here. If Verdana waits and Crestline is time-barred, Crestline can still offset.
- Cap: 11.2 caps liability at fees actually paid ($3,400,000), expressly excluding unpaid or change-order fees. This resolves the Board memo's ambiguity; estimated damages of $2,850,000 are under the cap. 11.1 excludes consequential damages; the $680,000 workaround costs may be attacked as consequential. 14.6 gives prevailing-party fees, which cuts both ways.

7. SOURCE-DOCUMENT INCONSISTENCIES TO FIX BEFORE LITIGATION
- Payment of the Phase 3 fee ($1,275,000): Amendment 4 and MSA 5.2 make it payable only on acceptance; every document says it was paid. Establish the payment date and basis. Crestline will argue acceptance by payment; Verdana's reservation-of-rights language (first notice) and 3.3 (no deemed acceptance of Phase 3) answer it.
- Acceptance Test Report misstates the MSA criteria (adds UAT 58 cases and a 200ms peak-load latency test; real Exhibit B uses average 200ms to 5,000 calls, 500ms at 10,000, 95th percentile 1,000ms, 60-minute sustained test, up to five Sev 2). Amendment Exhibit A item 3 states a 200ms 95th-percentile figure that conflicts with Exhibit B; Amendment 8 gives the Amendment priority. Crestline will exploit this on the merits.
- Section 3.4 process: Verdana used a 9.2 cure in lieu of the 3.4 deficiency report (30 days) and second test. Crestline may say the first failure was not a breach and that Verdana's acceptance process was not followed; the Jan 17-28, 2022 retest can be characterized as the second test. This helps accrual arguments for Verdana (later date) but invites a merits challenge.

8. RECOMMENDED ACTIONS (in order)
1. Today: send 14.1 notice and 14.5 mediation notice by courier and permitted email, proposing JAMS, with a 60-day clock; target delivery no later than mid-September 2022 to leave margin.
2. Retain New York litigation counsel now; prepare a complaint for filing in New York County no later than December 15, 2022 (internal deadline), and file by December 30, 2022 at the outside.
3. Re-offer Crestline a signed mutual tolling agreement (post-accrual, GOL 17-103, referencing 14.5 and 14.7); do not delay mediation while waiting for it.
4. Confirm the Phase 3 fee payment records and reservation-of-rights correspondence.
5. Reassess the Board's July 12 decision and update the Board on the corrected deadlines.

9. UNRESOLVED
- UCC versus services characterization and effect on accrual; enforceability of 14.7's knowledge-based accrual under a UCC theory.
- Whether 203(d) overrides the contractual period for Crestline's counterclaims.
- Texas four-year period used in the borrowing analysis not primary-source verified (Texas statute site was inaccessible).
- Operation of CPLR 205(a) on a contractual period.
- Whether Verdana's later acceptance-based accrual (January 28, 2022) will be accepted; treat as fallback only.
